first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the 4% completion decline and is supported by prior durable gains in completion, time-to-value, and activation. Promotional pricing addresses competitive pressure but carries a documented 30-day retention penalty that conflicts with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Verify the strongest action-relevant evidence and the key downside of the main alternative before committing.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified prior result directly matches the current 4% onboarding-completion decline and improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%, supporting sustainable qualified revenue. It may also help reverse the activation decline. Reject promotional pricing this cycle despite competitive pressure: verification confirms a 12% retention loss and failure before first renewal, which conflicts with the primary objective. Preserve uncertainty because the prior onboarding result may not fully replicate under current conditions.

final2.rationale: Continue with onboarding simplification. The competitor’s deeper cut and increased churn conversations raise urgency but do not overturn the verified economics: shortened onboarding improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, while targeted discounting produced a 12% retention decline and cohorts that failed before renewal. Matching the competitor with promotional pricing would therefore conflict with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Uncertainty remains because churn conversations are only an early signal and the prior discount test focused on acquisition rather than retention offers.
